body_text:
Pinot table conf and schema access is from restful API only right now.

It would be good to support the built-in system tables, and we can query schema in SQL style.
This will be useful for users to have a similar onboarding experience that everything can come from the query console. 
It's also good for Pinot integrations with other systems.

Query examples for references:
```
SHOW TABLES
```

```
DESCRIBE TABLE myTable
```


```
SHOW COLUMNS FROM myTable
```
 
```
SELECT 
    TABLE_SCHEMA,
    TABLE_NAME,
    COLUMN_NAME
FROM
    INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS
WHERE
    TABLE_SCHEMA <> 'INFORMATION_SCHEMA'
```
title: Support Describe Pinot table and schema

body_text:
Say we have the following event structure:

```json
{
	"...",
	"auditFields": {
		"a": "b",
		"c": "d"
	},
	"results": [
		{
			"name": "result1",
			"value": 33.2
		},
		{
			"name": "result2",
			"value": 45.6
		}
	]
}
```

We want to create the following columns:

```
results.name
results.value
auditFields
```

At the moment I don't think that's possible as auditFields will be flattened into:


```
audiFields.a
auditFields.c
```

By this line of code - https://github.com/apache/pinot/blob/master/pinot-segment-local/src/main/java/org/apache/pinot/segment/local/recordtransformer/ComplexTypeTransformer.java#L176

Can we make the columns that get flattened configurable, like the fields to unnest can be configured?
title: Choose which fields get flattened by complexType

body_text:
Currently `BOOLEAN` is supported using the `INT` data type, and `TIMESTAMP` is supported using the `LONG` data type. Even though the storage format are the same, the behavior should be different. E.g. reading `BOOLEAN` as `STRING` should give `"true"` or `"false"` instead of `1` or `0`; reading `DOUBLE` as `BOOLEAN` should give `doubleVal != 0` instead of `(int) doubleVal`.
In order to achieve the expected behavior, we need to add read APIs for these 2 data types. It should be similar to how the `BIG_DECIMAL` is handled (storage format is `BYTES`). We want to add type support in:
- Dictionary
- ForwardIndexReader
- BlockValSet
- TransformFunction
title: Add read APIs for `BOOLEAN` and `TIMESTAMP`

body_text:
Kinesis supports producing aggregated (aka batched) record. Thus, kinesis consumer also has support for de-aggregating the records. Refer - https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/kinesis-kpl-consumer-deaggregation.html 

Kinesis provides an `AggregatorUtil` (https://github.com/awslabs/amazon-kinesis-client/blob/master/amazon-kinesis-client/src/main/java/software/amazon/kinesis/retrieval/AggregatorUtil.java) that can be used in the `KinesisConsumer` implementation. An example usage of this util can be found in the beam repo (https://github.com/apache/beam/blob/master/sdks/java/io/amazon-web-services2/src/main/java/org/apache/beam/sdk/io/aws2/kinesis/SimplifiedKinesisClient.java#L269) 

Even though the records in the batch have the same sequence number, we can append the sub-sequence number to Pinot kinesis' `StreamMessageOffset`. Changes should be fairly trivial to do this. 

Labels: `enhancement` , `kinesis`, `help-wanted`

When new columns are added to a pinot table, the server is able to automatically generate default columns for the new added columns. There are 2 types of default column that can be auto-generated: 
1. New added column without transform function: default column will be filled with default null value (always dictionary encoded)
2. New added column with transform function (derived column): default column will be filled with values calculated based on the transform function

There are 2 things not handled right now:
1. Generate default column raw forward index (not dictionary encoded)
2. Support transform function on another new added column: we need to calculate the dependency between new added columns, and generate them in sequence

See `BaseDefaultColumnHandler` for details

Please provide a support reading the segment from bottom in this case, which can reduce the timetaken and numOfDocsScanned...

Thanks
Akram Syed

While writing some adhoc queries, I found the controller query console was throwing a 500 and I was scratching my head about the error until I realized the query was incorrect. I'm not sure if Pinot often 500s on invalid queries, or this is a corner case, but certainly making sure a helpful error is returned is better that informs the user their query is invalid.

For example, I was trying
```sql
select $segmentName, count(*)
from table
where $segmentName = 'bar'
```
Mind, the same error happened when I used actual columns rather than the virtual column.

And it was raising the following exception
```ProcessingException(errorCode:450, message:InternalError:
java.io.IOException: Failed : HTTP error code : 500

	at org.apache.pinot.controller.api.resources.PinotQueryResource.handlePostSql(PinotQueryResource.java:137))
```

body_text:
### Describe the bug

`HeadersDictProxy` deduplicates mapping keys with a case-sensitive set. HTTP header names are case-insensitive, and `CIMultiDict` keeps each insertion's original casing, so `X-Foo` and `x-foo` both appear in `list(headers)` / `len(headers)` even though `__getitem__` already joins them.

### To Reproduce

```python
from multidict import CIMultiDict
from aiohttp.helpers import HeadersDictProxy

md = CIMultiDict()
md.add("X-Foo", "1")
md.add("x-foo", "2")
md.add("Host", "a")
headers = HeadersDictProxy(md)

print(list(headers))  # ['X-Foo', 'x-foo', 'Host']
print(len(headers))   # 3
print(list(headers.items()))
# [('X-Foo', '1, 2'), ('x-foo', '1, 2'), ('Host', 'a')]
```

The same split keys show up on parsed request messages:

```python
# GET / HTTP/1.1 + Host: a + X-Foo: 1 + x-foo: 2
# list(msg.headers) == ['Host', 'X-Foo', 'x-foo']
# len(msg.headers) == 3
```

### Expected behavior

One mapping key per case-insensitive header name, keeping the first-seen casing:

```python
list(headers) == ['X-Foo', 'Host']
len(headers) == 2
list(headers.items()) == [('X-Foo', '1, 2'), ('Host', 'a')]
headers["x-foo"] == "1, 2"
```

### Related component

body_text:
### Describe the bug

`RequestHandler.start()` can call `self._request_factory` after `connection_lost()` has set it to `None`. The connection task then dies with an unretrieved exception that the event loop logs:

```
Task exception was never retrieved
future: <Task finished name='Task-9366' coro=<RequestHandler.start() done, defined at .../aiohttp/web_protocol.py:550> exception=TypeError("'NoneType' object is not callable")>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../aiohttp/web_protocol.py", line 594, in start
    request = self._request_factory(
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable
```

This happens when a request is queued (`data_received` appends to `_messages` and resolves `_waiter`) and `connection_lost()` runs in the same event-loop iteration, before `start()` resumes. `start()` then wakes from `await self._waiter`, sees a non-empty `_messages`, pops the message, and calls the cleared factory. The `while not self._force_close` check only runs at the top of the loop, so the `force_close()` inside `connection_lost()` isn't seen in time.

It's harmless in practice, because only the already-dead connection is affected. It does put a traceback into server logs, though, and a comment in 3.14.x says the post-`connection_lost` state is "not reachably exercisable" inside this loop. This reproduction shows that it is.

### To Reproduce

```python
import asyncio
from unittest import mock

import aiohttp
from aiohttp import web


async def main() -> None:
    async def handler(request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
        return web.Response(text="ok")

    proto = web.Server(handler)()
    transport = mock.Mock()
    transport.is_closing.return_value = False
    transport.get_extra_info.return_value = None
    proto.connection_made(transport)
    task = proto._task_handler
    await asyncio.sleep(0)  # start() is parked waiting for the next request

    # Same event-loop iteration: a request arrives, then the peer disconnects.
    proto.data_received(b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n")
    proto.connection_lost(None)

    for _ in range(5):
        await asyncio.sleep(0)
    print("aiohttp", aiohttp.__version__, "->", repr(task.exception()))


asyncio.run(main())
```

### Expected behavior

`start()` exits quietly once the connection is lost. That could be done by re-checking `self._force_close` (or `self._request_factory is None`) after the waiter resolves, before handling a popped message.

### Logs/tracebacks

```python-traceback
aiohttp 3.13.5 -> TypeError("'NoneType' object is not callable")
aiohttp 3.14.4 -> TypeError("'NoneType' object is not callable")
```

### Python Version

```console
Python 3.13.13
```

### aiohttp Version

```console
3.13.5 and 3.14.4 (latest), observed in production on 3.13.5
```

### OS

Windows 11 (ProactorEventLoop) in production. The reproduction above is event-loop agnostic.

### Related component

Server

This happens when a request is queued (`data_received` appends to `_messages` and resolves `_waiter`) and `connection_lost()` runs in the same event-loop iteration, before `start()` resumes. `start()` then wakes from `await self._waiter`, sees a non-empty `_messages`, pops the message, and calls the cleared factory. The `while not self._force_close` check only runs at the top of the loop, so the `force_close()` inside `connection_lost()` isn't seen in time.

It's harmless in practice, because only the already-dead connection is affected. It does put a traceback into server logs, though, and a comment in 3.14.x says the post-`connection_lost` state is "not reachably exercisable" inside this loop. This reproduction shows that it is.

from aiohttp import web


async def main() -> None:

        return web.Response(text="ok")

    transport = mock.Mock()
    transport.is_closing.return_value = False
    transport.get_extra_info.return_value = None
    proto.connection_made(transport)
    task = proto._task_handler
    await asyncio.sleep(0)  # start() is parked waiting for the next request

    # Same event-loop iteration: a request arrives, then the peer disconnects.
    proto.data_received(b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n\r\n")
    proto.connection_lost(None)

    for _ in range(5):
        await asyncio.sleep(0)
    print("aiohttp", aiohttp.__version__, "->", repr(task.exception()))


asyncio.run(main())
```

`start()` exits quietly once the connection is lost. That could be done by re-checking `self._force_close` (or `self._request_factory is None`) after the waiter resolves, before handling a popped message.

### Describe the bug

Since #11726, `WebSocketWriter.send_frame()` sends compressed frames larger than 16 KiB from a separate `send_task` and awaits it through `asyncio.shield()`. The only done-callback on that task is `self._background_tasks.discard`:

https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/blob/f17c631bddcfd4ec712342db28f1d3381a3fec71/aiohttp/_websocket/writer.py#L114-L117

If the task that called `send_str()` is cancelled while `send_task` is still running (for instance while the frame is being compressed in the executor) and the peer goes away in the meantime, `send_task` fails with `ClientConnectionResetError("Cannot write to closing transport")` and nothing retrieves that exception: `shield()` removes its done-callback from the inner task once the outer future is cancelled, and `discard` ignores the result. asyncio then reports it through the loop exception handler:

- Python 3.11 to 3.13: `Task exception was never retrieved`, when the task is garbage collected (measured on 3.11.0; 3.12 and 3.13 have the same `shield()` code);
- Python 3.14.0 to 3.14.8: `ClientConnectionResetError exception in shielded future`, logged by `shield()` itself (python/cpython#156321);
- the 3.14 branch after python/cpython#158599, which is not in 3.14.8: `Task exception was never retrieved` again.

So the 3.14 regression only changes the message. The unretrieved exception comes from the writer and is reported on all the versions above.

### To Reproduce

1. `pip install aiohttp==3.14.5`
2. Save the script below as `repro.py`.
3. Run `python repro.py cancel`, then `python repro.py nocancel`.

The handler sends a 64 KiB text message from a separate task, so it takes the compressed, shielded path, while a raw client negotiates `permessage-deflate` and drops the connection with a RST. The only patch to aiohttp is a 0.3 s delay in `ZLibCompressor.compress()`, so the peer is reliably gone by the time the frame is written; without it the race only triggers now and then. In `cancel` mode the handler cancels the sending task once the connection is closed; `nocancel` awaits it instead, as a control.

```python
"""The exception of the shielded compressed-send task is never retrieved when the
task calling send_str() is cancelled after the peer went away.

    python repro.py [cancel|nocancel]

cancel   : the task calling send_str() is cancelled once the connection is closed.
nocancel : control, the task calling send_str() is awaited instead.
"""

import asyncio
import base64
import gc
import os
import socket
import struct
import sys

import aiohttp
from aiohttp import web
from aiohttp._websocket import writer as ws_writer

MODE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "cancel"
logged = []
caller = []

# Frames larger than 16 KiB are compressed in an executor inside a shielded task.
# Delay the compression so the peer is reliably gone by the time the frame is
# written; without this the race only triggers occasionally.
_compress = ws_writer.ZLibCompressor.compress


async def slow_compress(self, data):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
    return await _compress(self, data)


ws_writer.ZLibCompressor.compress = slow_compress


async def handler(request: web.Request) -> web.WebSocketResponse:
    ws = web.WebSocketResponse()
    await ws.prepare(request)
    payload = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(48 * 1024)).decode()  # 64 KiB
    sender = asyncio.create_task(ws.send_str(payload))
    async for _ in ws:
        pass
    if MODE == "cancel":
        sender.cancel()
    try:
        await sender
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        caller.append("cancelled")
    except Exception as exc:
        caller.append(f"got {exc!r}")
    else:
        caller.append("no error")
    return ws


async def connect_and_reset(port: int) -> None:
    reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", port)
    key = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(16)).decode()
    writer.write(
        f"GET /ws HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:{port}\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\n"
        f"Connection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Key: {key}\r\n"
        "Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n"
        "Sec-WebSocket-Extensions: permessage-deflate\r\n\r\n".encode()
    )
    head = await reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")
    assert b" 101 " in head and b"permessage-deflate" in head.lower(), head
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    # Drop the connection with a RST while the server is still compressing.
    sock = writer.get_extra_info("socket")
    sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, struct.pack("ii", 1, 0))
    writer.transport.abort()


async def main() -> None:
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    loop.set_exception_handler(
        lambda _loop, ctx: logged.append(f"{ctx['message']}: {ctx.get('exception')!r}")
    )
    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_get("/ws", handler)
    runner = web.AppRunner(app)
    await runner.setup()
    site = web.TCPSite(runner, "127.0.0.1", 0)
    await site.start()
    await connect_and_reset(runner.addresses[0][1])
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    # "Task exception was never retrieved" is only reported once the task is collected.
    for _ in range(3):
        gc.collect()
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    await runner.cleanup()
    print(f"Python {sys.version.split()[0]}, aiohttp {aiohttp.__version__}, mode={MODE}")
    print(f"  caller           : {', '.join(caller) or '-'}")
    print(f"  logged by asyncio: {'; '.join(logged) or 'nothing'}")


asyncio.run(asyncio.wait_for(main(), 15))
```

| Python | `cancel` | `nocancel` (control) |
|---|---|---|
| 3.11.0 | `Task exception was never retrieved` | the caller gets the exception, nothing logged |
| 3.14.4 | `ClientConnectionResetError exception in shielded future` | the caller gets the exception, nothing logged |
| 3.14.4, `asyncio.tasks._log_on_exception` replaced by a no-op (what python/cpython#158599 removes) | `Task exception was never retrieved` | not run |

All with aiohttp 3.14.5; aiohttp 3.14.4 gives the same results on Python 3.14.4. Repeated runs give the same results.

### Expected behavior

When the task that called `send_str()` has been cancelled, nobody is left to receive the send error and the peer is already gone, so nothing should reach the loop exception handler. A caller that is not cancelled should keep getting the exception, as it does today.

### Additional context

A possible fix, in the spirit of `_ping_task_done()` (#8433): retrieve the exception in the done-callback of `send_task`. The diff is against v3.14.5; master has the same lines.

```diff
--- a/aiohttp/_websocket/writer.py
+++ b/aiohttp/_websocket/writer.py
@@ -113,7 +113,7 @@
                 send_task = asyncio.create_task(coro)
             # Keep a strong reference to prevent garbage collection
             self._background_tasks.add(send_task)
-            send_task.add_done_callback(self._background_tasks.discard)
+            send_task.add_done_callback(self._send_task_done)
             await asyncio.shield(send_task)
 
         # It is safe to return control to the event loop when using compression
@@ -128,6 +128,13 @@
             if self.protocol._paused:
                 await self.protocol._drain_helper()
 
+    def _send_task_done(self, task: "asyncio.Task[None]") -> None:
+        self._background_tasks.discard(task)
+        # The caller may have been cancelled while the shielded send was
+        # still running; nobody else will retrieve the exception then.
+        if not task.cancelled():
+            task.exception()
+
     def _write_websocket_frame(self, message: bytes, opcode: int, rsv: int) -> None:
         """
         Write a websocket frame to the transport.
```

With this patch applied to an installed aiohttp 3.14.5:

| Python | `cancel` | `nocancel` |
|---|---|---|
| 3.11.0 | nothing logged | the caller gets the exception, nothing logged |
| 3.14.4 | still `ClientConnectionResetError exception in shielded future` | the caller gets the exception, nothing logged |
| 3.14.4, `_log_on_exception` replaced by a no-op | nothing logged | not run |

  logged by asyncio: nothing
$ python repro.py cancel

  caller           : cancelled
  logged by asyncio: ClientConnectionResetError exception in shielded future: ClientConnectionResetError('Cannot write to closing transport')
$ python repro.py nocancel
Python 3.14.4, aiohttp 3.14.5, mode=nocancel
  caller           : got ClientConnectionResetError('Cannot write to closing transport')
  logged by asyncio: nothing
$ python -c "import asyncio.tasks, runpy, sys; asyncio.tasks._log_on_exception = lambda fut: None; sys.argv = ['repro.py', 'cancel']; runpy.run_path('repro.py', run_name='__main__')"
Python 3.14.4, aiohttp 3.14.5, mode=cancel

On 3.14.0 to 3.14.8 the remaining message comes from `shield()` itself: `_log_on_exception` logs the inner exception whether or not anything else retrieves it, so aiohttp can't silence it. It goes away with python/cpython#158599.

If you'd rather keep unexpected errors visible, the callback could pass anything that is not a `ConnectionError` to `loop.call_exception_handler()` instead of dropping it.

There is also a narrower window on 3.14.x. If the caller is cancelled after `send_task` has failed but before its done-callbacks have run, `shield()`'s inner callback returns early without retrieving the exception, so it is reported as `Task exception was never retrieved` even on 3.14.0 to 3.14.8. This is probably where the second message in the log above comes from; 3.11 retrieves the exception in that case. Forcing this window locally (a wrapper around `_send_compressed_frame_async_locked` cancels the caller just before re-raising) gives `Task exception was never retrieved` on 3.14.4 and nothing with the patch above; 3.11.0 logs nothing either way.

Related: #12281, fixed by #12307, the same kind of problem with `shield()` in `_drain_helper`.

Since #11726, `WebSocketWriter.send_frame()` sends compressed frames larger than 16 KiB from a separate `send_task` and awaits it through `asyncio.shield()`. The only done-callback on that task is `self._background_tasks.discard`:

https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/blob/f17c631bddcfd4ec712342db28f1d3381a3fec71/aiohttp/_websocket/writer.py#L114-L117

If the task that called `send_str()` is cancelled while `send_task` is still running (for instance while the frame is being compressed in the executor) and the peer goes away in the meantime, `send_task` fails with `ClientConnectionResetError("Cannot write to closing transport")` and nothing retrieves that exception: `shield()` removes its done-callback from the inner task once the outer future is cancelled, and `discard` ignores the result. asyncio then reports it through the loop exception handler:

- Python 3.11 to 3.13: `Task exception was never retrieved`, when the task is garbage collected (measured on 3.11.0; 3.12 and 3.13 have the same `shield()` code);
- Python 3.14.0 to 3.14.8: `ClientConnectionResetError exception in shielded future`, logged by `shield()` itself (python/cpython#156321);
- the 3.14 branch after python/cpython#158599, which is not in 3.14.8: `Task exception was never retrieved` again.

So the 3.14 regression only changes the message. The unretrieved exception comes from the writer and is reported on all the versions above.

### To Reproduce

1. `pip install aiohttp==3.14.5`
2. Save the script below as `repro.py`.
3. Run `python repro.py cancel`, then `python repro.py nocancel`.

The handler sends a 64 KiB text message from a separate task, so it takes the compressed, shielded path, while a raw client negotiates `permessage-deflate` and drops the connection with a RST. The only patch to aiohttp is a 0.3 s delay in `ZLibCompressor.compress()`, so the peer is reliably gone by the time the frame is written; without it the race only triggers now and then. In `cancel` mode the handler cancels the sending task once the connection is closed; `nocancel` awaits it instead, as a control.

```python
"""The exception of the shielded compressed-send task is never retrieved when the
task calling send_str() is cancelled after the peer went away.

    python repro.py [cancel|nocancel]

cancel   : the task calling send_str() is cancelled once the connection is closed.
nocancel : control, the task calling send_str() is awaited instead.
"""

import asyncio
import base64
import gc
import os
import socket
import struct
import sys

import aiohttp
from aiohttp import web
from aiohttp._websocket import writer as ws_writer

MODE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "cancel"
logged = []
caller = []

# Frames larger than 16 KiB are compressed in an executor inside a shielded task.
# Delay the compression so the peer is reliably gone by the time the frame is
# written; without this the race only triggers occasionally.
_compress = ws_writer.ZLibCompressor.compress


async def slow_compress(self, data):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
    return await _compress(self, data)


ws_writer.ZLibCompressor.compress = slow_compress


async def handler(request: web.Request) -> web.WebSocketResponse:
    ws = web.WebSocketResponse()
    await ws.prepare(request)
    payload = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(48 * 1024)).decode()  # 64 KiB
    sender = asyncio.create_task(ws.send_str(payload))
    async for _ in ws:
        pass
    if MODE == "cancel":
        sender.cancel()
    try:
        await sender
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        caller.append("cancelled")
    except Exception as exc:
        caller.append(f"got {exc!r}")
    else:
        caller.append("no error")
    return ws


async def connect_and_reset(port: int) -> None:
    reader, writer = await asyncio.open_connection("127.0.0.1", port)
    key = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(16)).decode()
    writer.write(
        f"GET /ws HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:{port}\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\n"
        f"Connection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Key: {key}\r\n"
        "Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n"
        "Sec-WebSocket-Extensions: permessage-deflate\r\n\r\n".encode()
    )
    head = await reader.readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")
    assert b" 101 " in head and b"permessage-deflate" in head.lower(), head
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    # Drop the connection with a RST while the server is still compressing.
    sock = writer.get_extra_info("socket")
    sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_LINGER, struct.pack("ii", 1, 0))
    writer.transport.abort()


async def main() -> None:
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    loop.set_exception_handler(
        lambda _loop, ctx: logged.append(f"{ctx['message']}: {ctx.get('exception')!r}")
    )
    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_get("/ws", handler)
    runner = web.AppRunner(app)
    await runner.setup()
    site = web.TCPSite(runner, "127.0.0.1", 0)
    await site.start()
    await connect_and_reset(runner.addresses[0][1])
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    # "Task exception was never retrieved" is only reported once the task is collected.
    for _ in range(3):
        gc.collect()
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    await runner.cleanup()
    print(f"Python {sys.version.split()[0]}, aiohttp {aiohttp.__version__}, mode={MODE}")
    print(f"  caller           : {', '.join(caller) or '-'}")
    print(f"  logged by asyncio: {'; '.join(logged) or 'nothing'}")


asyncio.run(asyncio.wait_for(main(), 15))
```

If you'd rather keep unexpected errors visible, the callback could pass anything that is not a `ConnectionError` to `loop.call_exception_handler()` instead of dropping it.

There is also a narrower window on 3.14.x. If the caller is cancelled after `send_task` has failed but before its done-callbacks have run, `shield()`'s inner callback returns early without retrieving the exception, so it is reported as `Task exception was never retrieved` even on 3.14.0 to 3.14.8. This is probably where the second message in the log above comes from; 3.11 retrieves the exception in that case. Forcing this window locally (a wrapper around `_send_compressed_frame_async_locked` cancels the caller just before re-raising) gives `Task exception was never retrieved` on 3.14.4 and nothing with the patch above; 3.11.0 logs nothing either way.

### Describe the bug

When a request with `Expect: 100-continue` is sent on a reused keep-alive connection, and the transport starts closing after the connection is taken from the pool but before the body-writer task runs, `writer.send_headers()` in `ClientRequest.write_bytes()` raises `ClientConnectionResetError('Cannot write to closing transport')`.

The request itself still succeeds (the caller sees no error), but the writer task's exception is never retrieved, so asyncio logs it through the loop exception handler:

```
Task exception was never retrieved
future: <Task finished name='Task-643' coro=<ClientRequest.write_bytes() done, defined at .../aiohttp/client_reqrep.py:1538> exception=ClientConnectionResetError('Cannot write to closing transport')>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../aiohttp/client_reqrep.py", line 1580, in write_bytes
    writer.send_headers()
  File ".../aiohttp/http_writer.py", line 239, in send_headers
    self._write(headers_buf)
  File ".../aiohttp/http_writer.py", line 103, in _write
    raise ClientConnectionResetError("Cannot write to closing transport")
aiohttp.client_exceptions.ClientConnectionResetError: Cannot write to closing transport
```

We see this about 550 times a day in production from botocore/aiobotocore S3 multipart uploads: botocore adds `Expect: 100-continue` to `UploadPart`, and our job leaves gaps of up to ~30 s between parts, so pooled connections are often closed by the peer around the time they are reused. All uploads succeed; only the log entry is produced.

### To Reproduce

```python
import asyncio
import gc
import os
import sys
import tempfile

import aiohttp
from aiohttp import web


async def handler(request: web.Request) -> web.Response:
    await request.read()
    return web.Response(text='ok')


async def main() -> None:
    reported = []
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    loop.set_exception_handler(lambda _loop, ctx: reported.append(f"{ctx['message']}: {ctx.get('exception')!r}"))

    sock = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), 's.sock')
    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_put('/', handler)
    runner = web.AppRunner(app)
    await runner.setup()
    await web.UnixSite(runner, sock).start()

    # Simulate the peer closing the idle connection right after the pool hands it out:
    # the close is scheduled from the reuse trace hook, so it runs before the
    # body-writer task created with create_task() gets its first step.
    async def on_reuse(_session, _ctx, _params) -> None:
        loop.call_soon(reused.transport.close)

    trace = aiohttp.TraceConfig()
    trace.on_connection_reuseconn.append(on_reuse)
    connector = aiohttp.UnixConnector(path=sock)
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=connector, trace_configs=[trace]) as session:
        async with session.put('http://localhost/', data=b'x') as resp:  # leaves one pooled connection
            await resp.read()

            await resp.read()
        print('2nd request: ok')

    await asyncio.sleep(0)

    await asyncio.sleep(0)

(`connector._conns` is only used to get hold of the pooled protocol for the simulation.)

No "Task exception was never retrieved". The request already recovers and succeeds, so the writer task's exception should be consumed by whoever owns the task.

- In `write_bytes()`, a failure in the 100-continue preamble is caught by the outer `except BaseException`, which closes the connection and re-raises, so the task ends with an exception.

### Describe the bug

`resp.content.total_raw_bytes` raises `AttributeError` when the response has no body, such as a 204 or a reply to HEAD. `EmptyStreamReader.__init__` skips `StreamReader.__init__`. It sets `total_bytes` but not `total_compressed_bytes`, which the property reads. #10386 was the same omission for `total_bytes`.

The property is documented as a read-only `int` at `docs/streams.rst:117`. A progress loop that reads it after the response ends fails on exactly the responses that have no body.

### To Reproduce

```python
import asyncio
import aiohttp
from aiohttp import web
from aiohttp.test_utils import TestServer

async def handler(request):
    return web.Response(status=204)

async def main():
    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_get("/", handler)
    async with TestServer(app) as server:
        async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
            async with session.get(server.make_url("/")) as resp:
                print("total_bytes     ", resp.content.total_bytes)
                print("total_raw_bytes ", resp.content.total_raw_bytes)

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Expected behavior

`total_raw_bytes` returns `0`, as `total_bytes` does.

### Logs/tracebacks

```python-traceback
total_bytes      0
  File ".../aiohttp/streams.py", line 262, in total_raw_bytes
    if self.total_compressed_bytes is None:
AttributeError: 'EmptyStreamReader' object has no attribute 'total_compressed_bytes'
```

### Python Version

```console
$ python --version
Python 3.12.6
```

### aiohttp Version

```console
$ python -m pip show aiohttp
Version: 3.14.5   # also master at 7275bea (4.0.0a2.dev0), pure Python
```

### multidict Version

```console
$ python -m pip show multidict
Version: 7.1.0
```

### propcache Version

```console
$ python -m pip show propcache
Version: 0.5.4
```

### yarl Version

```console
$ python -m pip show yarl
Version: 1.25.1
```

### OS

Linux

### Related component

Client

### Additional context

One line fixes it, next to the `total_bytes` line #10386 added: `self.total_compressed_bytes = None` in `EmptyStreamReader.__init__`. With it, the script above prints `0` for both on master at 7275bea.

I found it while reviewing #14078. The chunk hooks and `get_read_buffer_limits()` also raise there, but they need a different fix. Setting `_http_chunk_splits` would let `begin_http_chunk_receiving()` park a deque on the shared `EMPTY_PAYLOAD`, which `streams.py:617` guards against, so they want no-op overrides and constant limits. I'll keep those out of it.

@bdraco, I'm opening the one-liner with a 204 and HEAD test next.

{"key": "aio-libs/aiohttp#14098", "repository": "aio-libs/aiohttp", "issue_number": 14098, "github_issue_id": "5971543775", "url": "https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/issues/14098", "title": "EmptyStreamReader.total_raw_bytes raises AttributeError on a response with no body", "source_files": ["D:\OSS-Mentor\data\teacher_clickhouse\inventory_20261022T172108Z\issues_discovered.json"], "historical_labels": [], "beginner_difficulty_confirmed": false, "frozen": false, "decision": "availability_passed", "reason": "current_unassigned_no_observed_claim_or_open_pr", "open_pr_references": [], "claim_signals": [], "current_labels": [], "current_signal_group": "historical_signal_only", "body": "### Describe the bug

`resp.content.total_raw_bytes` raises `AttributeError` when the response has no body, such as a 204 or a reply to HEAD. `EmptyStreamReader.__init__` skips `StreamReader.__init__`. It sets `total_bytes` but not `total_compressed_bytes`, which the property reads. #10386 was the same omission for `total_bytes`.

The property is documented as a read-only `int` at `docs/streams.rst:117`. A progress loop that reads it after the response ends fails on exactly the responses that have no body.

### To Reproduce

```python
import asyncio
import aiohttp
from aiohttp import web
from aiohttp.test_utils import TestServer

async def handler(request):
    return web.Response(status=204)

async def main():
    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_get("/", handler)
    async with TestServer(app) as server:
        async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
            async with session.get(server.make_url("/")) as resp:
                print("total_bytes     ", resp.content.total_bytes)
                print("total_raw_bytes ", resp.content.total_raw_bytes)

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Expected behavior

`total_raw_bytes` returns `0`, as `total_bytes` does.

### Logs/tracebacks

```python-traceback
total_bytes      0
  File ".../aiohttp/streams.py", line 262, in total_raw_bytes
    if self.total_compressed_bytes is None:
AttributeError: 'EmptyStreamReader' object has no attribute 'total_compressed_bytes'
```

### Python Version

```console
$ python --version
Python 3.12.6
```

### aiohttp Version

```console
$ python -m pip show aiohttp
Version: 3.14.5   # also master at 7275bea (4.0.0a2.dev0), pure Python
```

### multidict Version

```console
$ python -m pip show multidict
Version: 7.1.0
```

### propcache Version

```console
$ python -m pip show propcache
Version: 0.5.4
```

### yarl Version

```console
$ python -m pip show yarl
Version: 1.25.1
```

### OS

Linux

### Related component

Client

### Additional context

One line fixes it, next to the `total_bytes` line #10386 added: `self.total_compressed_bytes = None` in `EmptyStreamReader.__init__`. With it, the script above prints `0` for both on master at 7275bea.

I found it while reviewing #14078. The chunk hooks and `get_read_buffer_limits()` also raise there, but they need a different fix. Setting `_http_chunk_splits` would let `begin_http_chunk_receiving()` park a deque on the shared `EMPTY_PAYLOAD`, which `streams.py:617` guards against, so they want no-op overrides and constant limits. I'll keep those out of it.

@bdraco, I'm opening the one-liner with a 204 and HEAD test next.

Recording a trade-off rather than reporting a defect, so it does not get
rediscovered every time someone compares the two.

`__setitem__()` is the one basic operation where `MultiDict` is
consistently behind `dict`, and the reason is structural. Instruction
counts from `benchmarks/callgrind_driver.py` on CPython 3.14.7, 200
`str` keys:

| Operation | `dict` | `MultiDict` | `CIMultiDict` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `d[key] = v`, existing key, GIL | 252 | 336 (+33%) | 422 (+67%) |
| `d[key] = v`, new key, GIL | 388 | 474 (+22%) | 560 (+44%) |
| `d[key] = v`, existing key, free-threaded | 344 | 515 (+50%) | 602 (+75%) |
| `d[key] = v`, new key, free-threaded | 525 | 667 (+27%) | 754 (+44%) |

For comparison, on the GIL build `MultiDict` is ahead of `dict` on
`d[key]` (150 against 184), `key in d` (134 against 174), `del d[key]`
(238 against 295) and `d.pop(key)` (428 against 476). The gap is
specific to the replace path.

CPython's `insertdict()` returns as soon as it finds the key.
`_md_replace()` in `_multilib/hashtable.h` cannot: `__setitem__()` on a
multi-value mapping has to replace the first entry for a key *and*
delete every later one, so it walks the rest of the probe chain even
when there is exactly one value. `md_del()` has the same shape for the
same reason.

Whether it can be improved comes down to knowing cheaply that a chain
holds no duplicates. The obvious counter, a per-object "has duplicates"
flag, is not free: `md_add()` would have to probe for an existing
identity to maintain it, and it deliberately does not probe today, so
the cost moves onto the operation `MultiDict` is currently fastest at.
Tracking a count of distinct identities has the same problem.

Filing this so the numbers and that dead end are written down. Happy to
close it as won't-fix if the trade-off is considered settled.

### Describe the feature

VIM motions enhancement: The most useful plugin, in my opinion, is Tim Pope's [vim-surround](https://github.com/tpope/vim-surround), which is already emulated by
[VS code](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=vscodevim.vim#-emulated-plugins) and [JetBrains' IDEs](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/33907396/how-can-i-use-vim-plugins-with-ideavim).


### Use Case

The limited Vim motion support is a persistent interruption to my coding experience which ultimately pushes me to look for alternatives.

### Proposed Solution

The most useful plugin, in my opinion, is Tim Pope's [vim-surround](https://github.com/tpope/vim-surround), which is already emulated by
[VS code](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=vscodevim.vim#-emulated-plugins) and [JetBrains' IDEs](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/33907396/how-can-i-use-vim-plugins-with-ideavim).

### Describe the bug

Search highlighting can make the editor very unresponsive when searching a large, heavily folded document.

### Expected Behavior

Editor should remain responsive independent of folded sections

### Current Behavior

Editor becomes unresponsive 

### Reproduction Steps

1. Open: https://sekedus.github.io/ace/kitchen-sink.html
2. Paste the contents of test.xodr.xml
3. Fold a lot of high level `<road>` elements (like 15-20)
4. Search for "Road" and scroll, the editor will be very unresponsive 

[test.xodr.xml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30163372/test.xodr.xml)

### Possible Solution

_No response_

_No response_

### Describe the feature

`src/lib/es6-shim.js` is still included in every build. It is loaded through
`src/lib/fixoldbrowsers.js`, which is required by `ace/loader_build`.

It polyfills 11 built-ins. All of them have been native in every major browser
since March 2017. Internet Explorer is the only browser that never got them.

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari | Edge |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `String.prototype.startsWith` | 41 | 17 | 9 | 12 |
| `String.prototype.endsWith` | 41 | 17 | 9 | 12 |
| `String.prototype.repeat` | 41 | 24 | 9 | 12 |
| `String.prototype.includes` | 41 | 40 | 9 | 12 |
| `Object.assign` | 45 | 34 | 9 | 12 |
| `Object.values` | 54 | 47 | 10.1 | 14 |
| `Array.prototype.find` | 45 | 25 | 8 | 12 |
| `Array.prototype.findIndex` | 45 | 25 | 8 | 12 |
| `Array.prototype.includes` | 47 | 43 | 9 | 14 |
| `Array.prototype.fill` | 45 | 31 | 8 | 12 |
| `Array.of` | 45 | 25 | 9 | 12 |

(Versions from `@mdn/browser-compat-data`.)

### Impact

- About 3.9 KB (unminified) in `src-noconflict/ace.js`.
- The block is byte-identical in v1.36.3, v1.43.3 and v1.44.0.
- In a current browser none of the `if (!X)` guards is true, so the code never runs.

### History

- The shim was added in #4720 ("Brought back from c9 branch"). No browser was named.
- A review comment in #4845 says the things used from `fixoldbrowsers` are already
  supported on all browsers ace supports.

### Question / proposal

Does ace still support Internet Explorer 11 or browsers older than 2017?

- If not: could `es6-shim.js` and `fixoldbrowsers.js` be removed from the default build?
- If yes: could the shim become opt-in (a separate file), so other users do not ship it?

I can open a PR if you agree with one of these.


### Use Case

It will reduce the size by ~ 4kb.

### Proposed Solution

_No response_

- [ ] This feature might incur a breaking change

Hi,
I'm almost sure this started since bumping to the new 0.17.0 version.
I am on Ubuntu 22.04 and using the i3 window manager. I use tmux. If I have multiple stacked windows on the same desktop - when I start from alacritty then switch to firefox browser then switch back to alacritty -- then 80% of the time the terminal will be stuck i.e. it won't accept input and won't respond to any keyboard press at all. The only thing that solves this is to exit alacritty and open it back. Since I use tmux that's fine since I always attach to the same session, but it's still very annoying.

If you need me to add some debug info please let me know how to do so - and I will gladly send it here.
Thanks!

 - JDK信息： openjdk17

### 重现步骤

```java
public static void main(String[] args) {
      String text = "这里放一个较大的json格式的字符串";
      JSONObject jsonObject = JSONObject.parseObject(text);
      System.out.println(jsonObject);

```

## 环境信息
- **fastjson2 版本**：2.0.61（当前最新稳定版）
- **JDK 版本**：JDK 25（Eclipse Adoptium 25.0.2）
- **操作系统**：Windows 11 / Linux（可按实际填写）
- **构建工具**：Maven / Gradle（可按实际填写）

## 问题描述
在 **JDK 25** 环境下，即使将 fastjson2 升级到 **最新稳定版 2.0.61**，运行时依然会持续打印 `sun.misc.Unsafe` 相关的废弃警告，具体日志如下：
```
WARNING: A terminally deprecated method in sun.misc.Unsafe has been called
WARNING: sun.misc.Unsafe::arrayBaseOffset has been called by com.alibaba.fastjson2.util.JDKUtils (file:/xxx/fastjson2-2.0.61.jar)
WARNING: Please consider reporting this to the maintainers of class com.alibaba.fastjson2.util.JDKUtils
WARNING: sun.misc.Unsafe::arrayBaseOffset will be removed in a future release
```
该警告在 JDK 23+ 开始强制输出，JDK 25 下依然存在，且**升级 fastjson2 到最新版无法解决**。

## 重现步骤
1. 配置项目依赖为 fastjson2 2.0.61：
